about:
I founded Ardagh Agencies in 2018 to address a growing need in the Irish commercial interiors sector for technically robust, sustainably manufactured architectural solutions.

Today, we represent a curated portfolio of advanced international manufacturers - including NARDI, NOWN, ONDARRETA, MORE THAN LAYERS, AECTUAL, and ARCHHYVE - delivering materials and systems that combine architectural integrity with circularity, bio-based innovation, and full material transparency.

Our work centres on supporting project teams - architects, designers, contractors, and developers - with clear specification guidance, sustainability alignment, and logistical coordination to ensure seamless adoption from concept through installation.

Alongside seven years of cross-sector experience spanning specification sales, digital systems, and project delivery, I hold a Diploma in Digital Business Analysis (Merit) from UCD Professional Academy and am currently studying Innovation for Sustainability at UCD Innovation Academy. This combination strengthens my ability to bridge technical performance, environmental responsibility, and modern digital workflows.

I bring a hybrid skill set that includes:

Specification sales and consultative project support
Sustainable materials expertise and regulatory alignment
CRM, pipeline management, and digital process optimisation
Experience across acoustics, furniture systems, and façade solutions

Increasingly, my focus is expanding into how sustainability-led decision making plays out beyond the built environment - particularly in areas like electric mobility, where real-world context, infrastructure, and user experience have a direct impact on adoption.

I’m driven by the intersection of material innovation, sustainability, and practical design delivery - and I collaborate closely with teams to add value at every stage of the product selection and procurement journey.

headline: Circular Design at Scale | Co-founder Aectual | Architect, Entrepreneur & Speaker
about:
Hedwig Heinsman is an architect and entrepreneur working at the intersection of architecture, technology and circularity. She is co-founder of Aectual, the global design-to-manufacture platform for 3D-printed circular architecture made from waste materials, dubbed “The Ultimate Upcycling Approach” by Forbes. Aectual works globally with leading brands including Hermès, Tiffany & Co. and Google.

In 2024, Aectual received the LVMH Innovation Award for Sustainability & Greentech, followed in 2026 by the World Economic Forum’s UpLink Low-Carbon and Circular Systems Challenge.

Previously, Heinsman co-founded DUS Architects, where she pioneered new forms of architecture and digital fabrication. Projects include the 3D Print Canal House, which was presented to then-President Barack Obama. The work of DUS received the prestigious Amsterdam Prize for the Arts and has been exhibited internationally at institutions including the V&A and the Rijksmuseum.

Heinsman graduated cum laude in Architecture from TU Delft and studied at Aalto University of Technology in Helsinki. She frequently speaks internationally on architecture, design and innovation, most recently at the World Economic Forum during Climate Week in New York, where she presented Aectual’s approach to circular architecture at scale. Her work and ideas have been featured by international media including BBC News, Al Jazeera, Frankfurter Allgemeine and Dutch Vogue.

Her current work explores what she calls Reincarnating Architecture: an approach in which architecture and its materials are not conceived as fixed or permanent, but can change, disappear and return in new forms. Her ongoing project Tiny Penthouses, first presented at the 19th International Architecture Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, explores this idea through adaptive architectural objects and installations responding to the housing challenges of contemporary cities.

about:
I'm a co-founder and CTO who builds technology that regulated, trust-critical industries can rely on.
 
My career has followed one thread: making complex systems trustworthy. I spent around a decade in mobile security engineering at Ericsson (cryptography, certificate handling and device protection), then led systems architecture at ST-Ericsson across multiple operating systems and customer programs. At Spotify I combined engineering leadership with governance, driving a company-wide IT General Controls program that reached across effectively the entire R&D organisation, and helping run the company-wide effort behind Spotify's 2018 NYSE direct listing. I then spent six years as CTO of Fishbrain, scaling a consumer platform and its data and machine-learning products to millions of users worldwide.
 
Today I'm co-founder and CTO of AI-BOB, where we bring AI to one of construction's hardest problems: turning complex, constantly-changing building regulations into automated, traceable compliance inside the tools designers already use. I own all of our technology, from architecture and engineering to the security and governance (including our ISO 27001-certified management system) that make our AI auditable and trustworthy, and I contribute as a founder across product, commercial and fundraising.

headline: cto @ alloovium (YC S26)
about:
Co-founder and CTO at Alloovium (YC S26). I dropped out to fix a problem I'd been staring at my whole life.
 
My father and brother are architects, so plans, specs, and building documents were basically the wallpaper of my childhood. I saw early that construction runs on paperwork, and that paperwork is a web, not a pile. A drawing depends on a spec. The spec depends on procedures and licences. All of it depends on promises made back in the tender. Change one detail without updating the rest, and nobody notices until it costs someone real time and money. Sometimes an auditor catches it. Sometimes a lawyer does. It's a big reason 80% of megaprojects blow their budget or schedule.
 
I went into software instead of architecture. Been building and shipping since I was a teenager, and I've learned more from the products that died than the ones that didn't. Two years into my degree, that old problem pulled me back. I dropped out, my co-founder Zander quit his civil engineering job, and we drove 26 hours to a new city to build Alloovium with no product and no customers.
 
Alloovium reads everything a construction project produces (contracts, specs, drawings, compliance records, conversations) and turns it into answers you can trust and compliance you can prove. Every answer cites the exact sentence it came from, and nothing AI-drafted moves without a human sign-off.
 
The bigger win is automating the workflows themselves. Take a daily site walk. Normally that's a superintendent's voice notes and photos sitting on their phone until someone gets around to writing it up, if they ever do. We pull that in daily and turn it into a weekly summary automatically, then check it against the project's management system and every other document connected to it. So instead of finding out a detail drifted six weeks and three documents too late, you know the week it happened.
 
We're now running across $400M+ of live projects, backed by Y Combinator and Startmate.
 
I never worked a site myself, so I do the next best thing: I sit in our customers' offices with the engineers who actually use this, and build around what they tell me, not what I assume.
 
If you want to build software that holds up on real projects, where a bug isn't cosmetic, come build with us.

projects.title: Gaussian Process State-Space Models for Nonlinear System Identification
projects.description:
Developed a Gaussian Process State-Space Model (GP-SSM) to identify and learn the dynamics of unknown, nonlinear systems. By combining expressive spectral-mixture Gaussian process priors with particle-filter inference, the model captures both smooth, data-driven transition dynamics and the uncertainty inherent in sequential observations. To handle state constraints (such as motion confined to a manifold) I applied the implicit function theorem to project particle samples onto the desired surface, ensuring physically consistent trajectories.

Through this project I deepened my understanding of Bayesian inference in dynamical systems, mastering Itô-calculus–based SDE solvers, variational approximations for intractable posteriors, and flexible kernel design. I also gained hands on experience implementing and tuning particle filters for high-dimensional state estimation. The resulting framework is broadly applicable for robotic control tasks requiring robust, uncertainty-aware policies, climate modeling and financial volatility forecasting.

Github: https://github.com/DevCielo/gaussian-process-state-space-models

projects.title: Real-Time Incremental Code Property Graph Engine
projects.description:
Built a production-grade Property Graph Engine that turned large codebases into rich Code Property Graphs (CPGs) and exposed them through a GraphRAG API for AI coding assistants like GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and Cody. The platform gave LLMs a structured, token-aware view of entire repositories, functions, classes, dependencies, call chains, and data flows, so they could answer questions and generate code with real architectural context instead of guessing from a single file.

Implemented a multi-language parsing pipeline using Tree-sitter to ingest Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and TSX, normalizing everything into a unified AST and then deriving control-flow graphs (CFG), program dependence graphs (PDG), call graphs, and higher-level CPG layers. Designed a high-performance storage layer on SQLite with aggressive indexing and caching to support sub-millisecond node lookups, fast 1–2 hop traversals, and pattern-matching queries for complex code patterns (e.g. multi-hop call chains, def-use relationships).

Engineered real-time, incremental graph updates with git-based change detection, surgical function-level reparsing, and a Kafka-backed streaming pipeline for exactly-once commit processing. Scaled the system horizontally via a coordinator + worker-node architecture with consistent hashing, per-partition graph databases, and Kubernetes/Helm deployment including autoscaling, Prometheus metrics, and Grafana dashboards. The result was a self-hosted, AI-ready code intelligence platform that sustained 10M+ LOC, <200 ms p50 GraphRAG queries, and 100+ commits/minute ingestion.

Github: https://github.com/DevCielo/property-graph.git

Implemented core NeRF foundations (volume rendering, ray marching, positional encodings), advanced variants (Mip‑NeRF, Instant‑NGP hash encodings), and an anisotropic Gaussian splatting renderer with adaptive density control and spherical harmonics. Designed a conversion algorithm to extract 3D Gaussians from trained NeRFs with progressive LOD controls. Delivered web/mobile demos featuring live SLAM capture and AR/VR plugins for Unity/Unreal, containerized via Docker for scalable deployments.
Through this project I mastered volumetric rendering algorithms, GPU pipeline optimization, and research‑to‑production workflows—deepening expertise in PyTorch, CUDA, OpenGL/WebGL and real‑time graphics programming.
The resulting system produces high‑fidelity, real‑time 3D scenes suited for robotics, VR/AR applications, gaming, autonomous‑vehicle mapping, and film‑quality VFX.

projects.title: Crime Script Analysis Research Project
projects.description:
Working alongside a team of six to develop a causality-aware Graph Neural Network (GNN) model for crime script analysis. My role focuses on overseeing the reinforcement learning module and driving the design of the GNN model architecture to extract and interpret causal relationships from complex crime data. The project integrates choke points (environmental constraints) and pinch points (critical offender decision-making moments) to reveal the underlying dynamics of criminal events. More specifically my roles include:

- Designing and integrating a GNN model that distinguishes between correlation and causation in crime event sequences.
- Developing methodologies for extracting causal links using advanced graph representation techniques, including the incorporation of Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) principles.
- Extracting Subject-Verb-Object (SVO) relationships and key event indicators from unstructured crime reports.
- Building robust data pipelines for cleaning, parsing, and structuring free-text data into actionable crime event graphs. 
- Contributing to the sentiment analysis module to capture emotional nuances and contextual insights from crime narratives.
- Enhancing model interpretability by integrating environmental (choke point) and behavioral (pinch point) features.
- Guiding the exploration of reinforcement learning approaches to simulate counterfactual scenarios and identify strategic intervention points.
- Providing technical guidance on embedding complex relational data into the GNN framework, ensuring the model accurately reflects the underlying investigative logic.
- Collaborating with domain experts to validate model assumptions and maintain alignment with real-world crime investigation needs.

projects.title: Decoding Neural Networks

By reimplementing classic neural network architectures, such as LeNet-5 and AlexNet, I gained a deep understanding of both the high-level concepts and the core mathematical operations that power these models. The project involves three implementation strategies: two versions using TensorFlow and PyTorch for efficient, production-level code and another built from scratch using NumPy to delve into the underlying mechanics of neural networks.

Throughout the project, I learned how to translate the complex ideas presented in research papers into functional code. This hands-on approach not only deepened my knowledge of neural network architectures but also honed my skills in debugging and problem-solving. By working with real-world datasets, I was able to see firsthand how these models operate in practical scenarios, which further solidified my understanding of their applications. publications.title: GB2573219 - Method and computer programs for identifying differences between 3-dimensional scenes
publications.description:
The present invention relates to three-dimensional modeling of complex objects, and in particular to the detection of differences between different scenes or different versions of a scene. 

Being able to reliably establish what has changed between two revisions of the same 3D scene, or even between two entirely different 3D scenes, has numerous applications across various industries. These range from Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) through to games development and medical imaging. For example, Computer Aided Design (CAD) and Building Information Modeling (BIM) rely heavily on 3D models that change over time as the designs evolve. The myriad of editing tools and ever growing collaborative teams make it extremely difficult to keep track of frequent changes in 3D space. Despite being the norm in software development, version control and change detection are not prevalent in 3D modeling workflows even when the design teams are all utilizing the same authoring toolset.

publications.title: 3drepo. io: building the next generation Web3D repository with AngularJS and X3DOM
publications.description: This paper presents a novel open source web-based 3D version control system positioned directly within the context of the recent strategic plan for digitising the construction sector in the United Kingdom. The aim is to achieve reduction of cost and carbon emissions in the built environment by up to 20% simply by properly managing digital information and 3D models. Even though previous works in the field concentrated mainly on defining novel WebGL frameworks and later on the efficiency of 3D data delivery over the Internet, there is still the emerging need for a practical solution that would provide ubiquitous access to 3D assets, whether it is for large international enterprises or individual members of the general public. We have, therefore, developed a novel platform leveraging the latest open web-based technologies such as AngularJS and X3DOM in order to define an industrial-strength collaborative cloud hosting service 3drepo.io. Firstly, we introduce the work and outline the high-level system architecture as well as improvements in relation to previous work. Next, we describe database and front-end considerations with emphasis on scalability and enhanced security. Finally, we present several performance measurement experiments and a selection of real-life industrial use cases. We conclude that jQuery provides performance benefits over AngularJS when manipulating large scene graphs in web browsers.

publications.title: 3D Timeline: Reverse Engineering of a Part-based Provenance from Consecutive 3D Models
publications.description: We present a novel tool for reverse engineering of modeling histories from consecutive 3D files based on a timeline abstraction. Although a timeline interface is commonly used in 3D modeling packages for animations, it has not been used on geometry manipulation before. Unlike previous visualization methods that require instrumentation of editing software, our approach does not rely on pre-recorded editing instructions. Instead, each stand-alone 3D file is treated as a keyframe of a construction flow from which the editing provenance is reverse engineered. We evaluate this tool on six complex 3D sequences created in a variety of modeling tools by different professional artists and conclude that it provides useful means of visualizing and understanding the editing history. A comparative user study suggests the tool is well suited for this purpose.

publications.title: XML3DRepo: A REST API for Version Controlled 3D Assets on the Web
publications.description: Current Web 3D technologies are not yet fully exploiting the modern design patterns for accessing online resources such as REST. XML3DRepo is a novel fusion of XML3D and 3D Repo. XML3D is an open source extension to HTML that supports interactive 3D graphics in WebGL-enabled browsers. 3D Repo is a recent versioning framework for 3D assets that provides raw access to its NoSQL database. XML3DRepo, in turn, is a server-side combination of the two technologies that stores a unified file format independent representation of 3D scenes in its repository but exposes a RESTful API for a deeper integration with other services using a variety of encodings selected between by the client application. First, we outline the overall architecture of the system and provide a simple yet powerful API definition that we believe has the potential to accommodate crowdsourcing of 3D models in the future. Next, we describe different 3D data encoding strategies for the Web and evaluate several of these for their speed and efficiency in our open source prototype implementation of the proposed API. We conclude that none of the formats strike the right balance between the number of requests, decoding overhead and the compression achieved making the proposed flexible architecture even more compelling.

publications.title: Visualizing 3D Models in Aid of Public Consultation
publications.publishedAt: SIGGRAPH Asia 2012 Symposium on Apps · Dec 1, 2012
publications.description: We present a novel approach to visualizing 3D models in aid of public consultation. 3D assets of architectural and engineering proposals are decomposed into individual constituents and uploaded to a NoSQL database (DB). A newly developed Android application visualizes such centrally stored assets on mobile devices. Localized comments are pushed back to the DB for subsequent analysis. This concept is expected to improve the public engagement and significantly reduce the costs of running such events.

publications.title: 3D Diff: An Interactive Approach to Mesh Differencing and Conflict Resolution
publications.description: We present an open source tool, 3D Diff, that supports differencing and merging of 3D models. As modeling software grows in use, and as 3D models get more complex and require input from more users, there is an emerging problem of maintaining large scenes over time. A scene might be concurrently edited by different users and thus there is a need to merge different versions of a 3D model. We frame this problem in a way that is analogous to software merging: firstly, we automatically detect differences in 3D models by noting correspondences and discrepancies between them; secondly we provide an interactive tool to select between such changes in order to effect a merge. To achieve this we introduce the notions of explicit and implicit conflicts in 3D models and develop a prototype implementation to support the differencing and merging processes. We evaluate this tool with users and find the 3D Diff to be an effective way of merging 3D models. We claim that such tools have an important role to play in the maintenance of large models.

publications.title: 3D Diff: An Interactive Approach to Mesh Differencing and Conflict Resolution
publications.description: We introduce 3D diff, a novel approach to interactively resolve conflicting mesh edits. Our method performs conflict detection and visualization and allows the user to quickly select one of the two revisions for each conflicted scene graph (SG) node. By further integrating the knowledge about a common ancestor of the two models, a. k. a. 3-way diff, we are able to automatically resolve more conflicts than in a standard 2-way comparison. Our method is particularly useful for revision management of 3D models.

publications.title: 3D Revision Control Framework
publications.description: The maintenance of assets in a large 3D scene can involve many authors with potentially different skills and different modeling tools. The standard paradigm of collaborative editing is sharing of files between various instances of applications. This presents problems, not limited to maintaining consistency of the models and dealing with concurrent edits in the same part of a scene. In this paper, we present a novel framework for non-linear revision control and online distribution of 3D assets. This framework supports concurrent asynchronous 3D editing of models and tracking of multiple revisions so that they can be integrated at a later date. It thus provides similar functionality to file-based revision control systems, but is built around a NoSQL database, hence avoids the constraints of file based storage. The framework supports distributed editing over the Internet and additional lightweight clients in web-browsers with WebGL support.

publications.title: Revision Control Framework for 3D Assets
publications.description: We propose a non-linear concurrent revision control for centralised management of 3D assets and a novel approach to mesh differencing. Large models are decomposed into individual scene graph (SG) nodes through an asset import library and become versioned as collections of polymorphic documents in a NoSQL database (DB). Well-known operations such as 2- and 3-way diff and merging are supported via a custom DB front-end. By not relying on the knowledge of user edits, we make sure our system works with a range of editing software. We demonstrate the feasibility of our proposal on concurrent 3D editing and conflict resolution.
